newsitem.title: USA: U.S. House approves $12 billion transport bill.
newsitem.headline: U.S. House approves $12 billion transport bill.

text.p: The U.S. House of Representatives on Wednesday passed by a 424-5 vote a $12.48 billion transportation spending bill for fiscal 1998, including a nearly 20 percent increase in highway spending and new air safety initiatives.
The bill was very close to President Bill Clinton's $12.47 billion budget request, and was $400 million above spending in the current fiscal year.
The bill includes funding for the Federal Aviation Administration to, among other things, install new airport security devices and improve storm and weather detection systems.
It also adds 500 air traffic controllers, and 326 FAA staff for safety certification and regulation.
The bill also would add money for the Coast Guard's efforts to combat drug trafficking, and targets Amtrak funding to improve the Northeast corridor.

The General Aviation Manufacturers Association said the House bill provided more funding for the FAA than requested by the Clinton administration, while rejecting the president's request for aviation user fees and limiting future consideration of such fees.
"This action refutes those who contend that user fees are necessary to provide the FAA with sufficient resources," GAMA President Ed Bolen said.
